dossier.public_summary: The dip is not steady between TESS sectors and between transits — two transits are very deep and two others are consistent with zero — so a single source on the target cannot explain it. With a nearby star close enough to fake the dip and no centroid to put it on the target, a blended eclipsing binary or systematics is the best explanation.

reasons.why: Depth changes by 187.3% between sectors: 11407, -424 and 7965 ppm with chi2 75.02 dof 2. Sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source with TESS-SPOC p_constant 1.4373238911572035e-15.

Individual transit depths inconsistent: epochs -2 11445 ppm sigma 4.7 and -1 11365 ppm sigma 4.4 versus epoch 0 -346 ppm sigma -5.1 and epoch 1 -509 ppm sigma -5.0. Signal driven by two very deep events only.

One neighbour within 1 TESS pixel could produce the dip with a 25% eclipse, and 12 neighbours could cause it. Centroid_all verdict inconclusive with no sector with a clear difference image, so off-target blended binary cannot be ruled out.

Scorer ranks this as planet-like as only 15% of known planets, supported by sector-depth non-constancy and inconsistent transits. Shape v_sigma -3.171 flat bottom and size rp_rearth 3.438 are positively planet-like but are outweighed by false-positive indicators.
